claim: Late delivery sharply increases bad reviews
key_number: Bad-review (1-2 star) rate 62.42% late vs 9.25% on time; gap 53.17 pp (95% CI 51.96-54.37)
caveat: Observational: "increases" means "goes with"; reviewed orders only (95,560)

claim: Late delivery accounts for a large share of all bad reviews (ESTIMATE)
key_number: 3,391.2 excess bad reviews = 27.73% of all 12,228 bad reviews
caveat: Assumes late orders would otherwise have been reviewed at the on-time rate (9.25%)

claim: Excess bad reviews are concentrated in a few states and routes (ESTIMATE)
caveat: Each group uses its own on-time baseline, so group excesses do not add up; RJ and SP are also the largest states

claim: A few sellers cause a large share of late orders / excess bad reviews
key_number: Top 20 of 411 sellers = 24.78% of national excess bad reviews; worst 10% of sellers = 11.42% of all late orders
caveat: Concentration is real but moderate; most late orders come from the many other sellers

key_number: 180-day repeat 1.58% late vs 2.01% on time; diff -0.43 pp (CI -0.80 to +0.02), p = 0.062
caveat: Not proof of zero: power was 50% for the observed gap
Whether the score matters at all is not significant after Holm

claim: Retention is structural: the first-order experience explains almost none of who returns
caveat: Only measures what is in the data; "structural" = not explained by delivery or review experience

claim: Distance (cross-state shipping) increases lateness and delivery time
key_number: Late 8.07% cross-state vs 4.51% same state; median 12.78 vs 6.52 days
caveat: Same state is a rough proxy for distance; association only

claim: Freight share is not a driver of lower repeat buying
key_number: Repeat by freight band 1.82-2.19%, no pattern; adjusted OR 1.13 per +10 pp (positive)
caveat: Not "no association": higher share goes with slightly more repeat buying, likely basket type
State rankings should not drive retention decisions

claim: Repeat rates differ by first-order category
caveat: Only read differences with non-overlapping CIs

claim: Faster delivery goes with slightly more repeat buying
key_number: OR 0.892 per extra week of delivery time (CI 0.828-0.960), Model A
caveat: Small, exploratory effect; overlaps with lateness
